featuresWeLack: [ADOPT] Zero-config paste deploy: the whole product is one _worker.js pasted into the CF dashboard (or main.zip uploaded to Pages); the only required settings are an ADMIN password variable and a KV namespace bound as KV, plus a custom domain — no build, no wrangler, no config file (https://github.com/cmliu/edgetunnel#quick-deployment)

[ADOPT] Live runtime config: the admin panel writes settings into KV and they take effect immediately without redeploy; env vars override KV in a two-tier merge (readConfig_JSON()) (https://deepwiki.com/cmliu/edgetunnel; https://edt-pages.github.io/admin)
[GAP] XHTTP and gRPC transports (gun/multi modes, gRPC UA) alongside WebSocket; Q Proxy is WS-only (https://edt-pages.github.io/admin; https://deepwiki.com/cmliu/edgetunnel)

[GAP] PATH-based dynamic egress switching per request: /proxyip=X, /?proxyip=X, /socks5=user:pass@host:port, /socks://base64, /http=..., /trojan=ip:port (fallback mode) (https://github.com/cmliu/edgetunnel#-advanced-tips)

[GAP] Preferred-IP subsystem ('addip' instinct): custom ADD list edited in the panel, 'random preferred' mode that picks per-subscriber-network official CF IPs at sub time, external preferred-sub generator mode (BEST_SUB) so one deployment can serve copy-ready preferred subs, and port picker over the CF TLS port family (https://edt-pages.github.io/admin; https://github.com/cmliu/edgetunnel README BEST_SUB)

[GAP] Per-colo default ProxyIP: when env.PROXYIP is unset the worker derives '<colo>.<code>.<code>SsSs.net' so a fresh deploy tunnels out of the box without any proxy IP research (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js)

[GAP] External subconverter integration: /sub renders native mixed/base64 only and delegates Clash/SingBox/Surge/QX/Loon to a SUBAPI backend with a daily-rotating token, plus tunables (config URL, emoji, UDP, XUDP, TLS1.3, sort) (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js; sponsored backend https://sub.cmliussss.net/)

[ADOPT] Subscription UX headers: Profile-Update-Interval, Profile-web-page-url (/admin), and Subscription-Userinfo derived from the CF usage API (upload/download/total/expire) (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js)

[ADOPT] Client onboarding inside the panel: QR codes + one-click copy for node link / adaptive / Base64 / Clash / SingBox subs, a beginner mode ('I'm a noob! I want it simple!'), one-click config reset, and live network self-tests (CN / non-CN / CF-ProxyIP / Google) with an explainer of which setting controls which test (https://edt-pages.github.io/admin)

[ADOPT] Operational introspection: operation-log viewer persisted in KV with a 4MB auto-prune, Workers/Pages daily request usage vs the 100k quota with 08:00 UTC+8 reset countdown, Telegram bot push notifications (https://edt-pages.github.io/admin)

[GAP] Node-level client-compat knobs exposed in UI: TLS fragmentation presets (Shadowrocket/Happ), 0-RTT ed=2560, random fake WS path, ECH with DoH/ECH-domain presets, fingerprint presets (chrome/firefox/safari/ios/android/edge/360/qq/random), allowInsecure toggle (https://edt-pages.github.io/admin)

[ADOPT] Quick-sub vanity path: GET /<KEY> 302-redirects to /sub?token=MD5MD5(host+userID) so the share URL never exposes the token (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js; https://github.com/cmliu/edgetunnel README KEY row)

[GAP] Transport perf engineering visible in source: 8KB WS early data, 20KB uplink coalescing target (16MB/4096-entry queue caps), 32KB downlink grain packing with low-watermark, configurable TCP concurrent dial (auto single-dial on CMCC), proxy concurrent dial, optional preload race dial (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js; https://github.com/cmliu/edgetunnel README env table)
[GAP] Camouflage homepage: URL env var proxies a decoy page (or 1101 error page) on the root path (https://github.com/cmliu/edgetunnel README URL row)
[GAP] /version fuzzy-UUID endpoint letting clients check deployed worker version for update prompts (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js)
featuresWeWin: Real admin authentication: PBKDF2 (100k iter, legacy 15k auto-upgrade) password tiers, HMAC-signed q_session {exp,iat} cookies with a KV revocation floor (qproxy:min-iat), and CSRF enforcement via X-Q-Panel header — vs edgetunnel's plaintext password compare, MD5MD5(UA + KEY + password) cookie whose KEY defaults to a hard-coded string constant, UA-bound 24h cookie, no CSRF token, no rate limit, no revocation short of rotating env vars (E:/code/Q Proxy AGENTS.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js)

Per-user model: up to 50 scoped users with per-user sub tokens, protocol filters, daily quotas, and expiry — vs edgetunnel's single shared UUID where the sub token is MD5MD5(host + userID) and userID is printed in every vless:// share link, so the tunnel credential doubles as the subscription credential by design (E:/code/Q Proxy AGENTS.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js; https://github.com/cmliu/edgetunnel README advanced tips section tying ADMIN/KEY rotation to both token and UUID)
WARP/WireGuard serving: account management, presets, amnezia, 17 output formats — edgetunnel has no WARP feature at all (E:/code/Q Proxy AGENTS.md)

Kill-switch gate before WebSocket upgrade and SSRF guards on dohUpstream/remoteDns/camouflage/remoteSubUrls/egress targets — absent from edgetunnel, which trusts any path/query-supplied proxyip/socks5 target (E:/code/Q Proxy AGENTS.md)

Native pure-function emitters (clash-yaml, singbox-json, surge-conf, loon-conf + base64) so client configs never leave the worker and no third-party converter ever sees node UUIDs/addresses — vs edgetunnel shipping raw node data through an operator-controlled SUBAPI backend (E:/code/Q Proxy AGENTS.md ADR-004; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js)

Protocol correctness discipline: parsers never throw (ParseResult/PushOutcome), SS SIP004 little-endian nonce with LE test helper, first-packet-consumed-once, Trojan UDP ATYP framing, port/security pairing invariant enforced by address-composition tests — edgetunnel has no test suite in evidence (E:/code/Q Proxy AGENTS.md)

Governed configuration: 66-leaf validated settings via descriptor table with interface/registry/dictionary drift tests, validateSettings-before-saveSettings, TOCTOU re-check on setup — vs free-form KV JSON merged with a 9-way env fallback chain that even accepts env.UUID as the admin password (E:/code/Q Proxy AGENTS.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js)

Auditable engineering: strict TypeScript, zero runtime dependencies, named modules with frozen ARCHITECTURE contracts and ADRs, CI typecheck + unit/workers vitest — vs one obfuscated Chinese-identifier JS file containing a 'kill-detection feature-code dictionary' (charcode-built 'PROXYIP'/'cmliu'/'722100' strings to evade scanners) and an embedded multilingual essay addressed at automated classifiers asserting 'no hidden backdoors... users can trust this code', both observed in fetched source (E:/code/Q Proxy AGENTS.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js)

Bilingual EN/FA panel with sensitive fields (passwordHash/salt, sessionSecret, botToken) excluded from responses, plus login throttling and bounded replay registries — edgetunnel logs requests to KV including IPs with only an opt-out env var (E:/code/Q Proxy AGENTS.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js OFF_LOG row)
panel: cmliu/edgetunnel is the dominant single-file Cloudflare Workers/Pages proxy panel (44,432 stars / 36,532 forks, GPL-2.0, fork of zizifn/edgetunnel created 2020-12-12 with 8,923 stars but 48,056 forks — the fork-to-star ratio itself documents the copy-paste deploy spread) (https://github.com/cmliu/edgetunnel; https://github.com/zizifn/edgetunnel). The ancestor zizifn project was "Running V2ray inside edge/serverless runtime": a hand-rolled JS VLESS-over-WS implementation born because V2ray is Go-based and cannot run on V8 runtimes; it supported TCP + DNS-over-UDP only, explicitly no VMess ("too complex") and no general UDP, and exposed exactly three routes: / (CF metadata), /{UUID} (returns VLESS config info — the original UUID-path subscription), everything else 404 (https://deepwiki.com/zizifn/edgetunnel; https://web.archive.org/web/20230601000000/https://edgetunnel.114567.xyz/). Its README was gutted in May 2023 ("delete readme" commit 13fb9eb, https://api.github.com/repos/zizifn/edgetunnel/commits?path=README.md) leaving a stub, so cmliu's fork is where the product evolved. cmliu 2.1 keeps the single-file _worker.js model but adds: an /admin panel (a static SPA fetched from https://edt-pages.github.io that the worker proxies), cookie login against an ADMIN env password, KV-backed runtime config, VLESS+Trojan+Shadowsocks, WS/gRPC/XHTTP transports, preferred-IP ("youxuan") subscription generation, and subconverter-delegated Clash/SingBox/Surge/Loon/QX output (https://github.com/cmliu/edgetunnel; https://deepwiki.com/cmliu/edgetunnel; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js). Deploy is deliberately trivial: paste _worker.js into a Worker (or upload main.zip to Pages / connect the fork), add one ADMIN variable, bind a KV namespace named KV, attach a domain, log in at /admin (https://github.com/cmliu/edgetunnel#quick-deployment). Its genius is the deploy-and-it-works instinct — everything else (per-colo default ProxyIP domain, UUID auto-derived as MD5MD5(ADMIN+KEY), no-ADMIN decoy page, UA-negotiated subs) works with zero configuration (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js). Its cost is a weak security model: MD5-of-password cookies with UA bound in, no CSRF, no rate limiting, one shared UUID, subscription token derivable from any node share link, and code that deliberately obfuscates identifiers from scanners plus an embedded multilingual "this file is legitimate, no hidden backdoors" essay addressed at automated code classifiers, both present in fetched _worker.js source (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js).
screens: /login — password-only form served from the static Pages host (edt-pages.github.io/login); POST compares plaintext against env password and sets cookie auth=MD5MD5(UA+KEY+password), 24h Max-Age, HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Lax; correct cookie on /login redirects to /admin; visiting /logout or a UUID-shaped path clears the cookie (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js)

/admin — single settings page, all sections on one scroll (no multi-page IA), SPA loaded from https://edt-pages.github.io/admin with header actions: beginner mode toggle, reset-config, logout (https://edt-pages.github.io/admin)
/admin section: Workers/Pages request usage dashboard — daily quota 100,000, usage %, reset countdown to 08:00 Beijing time (https://edt-pages.github.io/admin)

/admin section: current network self-tests — CN test, non-CN test, CF/ProxyIP egress IP, Google, each annotated with which config controls it (routing rules vs preferred IPs vs PROXYIP) (https://edt-pages.github.io/admin)

/admin section: get node links — node link format display, QR code, one-click copy for adaptive subscription, Base64 subscription, Clash subscription, SingBox subscription (https://edt-pages.github.io/admin)

/admin section: preferred-IP subscription generation ('addip' UI) — three modes (preferred-sub generator 'copy homework', random preferred IPs auto-matched to the subscriber's ISP at request time, custom/merged subscriptions), preferred count, TLS port picker (443/2053/2083/2087/2096/8443), custom preferred-IP list editor, chained-proxy option (https://edt-pages.github.io/admin)

/admin section: detailed config — sub name, HOST, UUID, PATH, node protocol VLESS/Trojan, SS cipher (aes-128-gcm / aes-256-gcm), TLS on/off, transport WebSocket/XHTTP/gRPC, gRPC mode gun/multi + UA, fingerprint presets, skip-cert-verify, random fake path, 0-RTT ed=2560, TLS fragmentation for Shadowrocket/Happ (https://edt-pages.github.io/admin)

/admin section: ECH (Encrypted Client Hello) — enable toggle, EchConfig DoH service presets (OpenDNS/Quad9/NextDNS/Ali/Tencent-SM2/360/OneDNS/custom), EchConfig resolution domain presets (https://edt-pages.github.io/admin)

/admin section: Cloudflare CDN access settings — reverse-proxy mode PROXYIP (with auto-acquire toggle), SOCKS5/HTTP upstream with credentials, per-entry global-proxy toggles, path template config, external 'get more PROXYIP/SOCKS5/HTTP/HTTPS' picker links (https://edt-pages.github.io/admin)
/admin section: subconverter config — backend URL (SUBAPI), converter config file URL, emoji, node-info-only, UDP, XUDP, TLS 1.3, append node type, sort order (https://edt-pages.github.io/admin)
/admin section: notifications — Telegram bot notification enable + params; Cloudflare Workers/Pages usage-statistics push config (https://edt-pages.github.io/admin)
/admin section: operation log viewer — KV-persisted request logs, auto-pruned at 4MB (https://edt-pages.github.io/admin)

noADMIN decoy — when no admin password env is set, non-WS requests serve a static 'noADMIN' page with 404 status instead of a panel (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js)

/sub?token=... — tokenized subscription endpoint (not a UI page): token = MD5MD5(host+userID) or a daily-rotating converter token; format chosen by ?target=, then ?clash/?sb/?singbox/?surge/?quanx/?loon flags, then UA sniffing (clash|meta|mihomo, sing-box, surge, quantumult, loon), default mixed; ?sub=<url> merges external subs; GET /<KEY> redirects here with a fresh token (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js)

ancestor /{UUID} page — zizifn-era: visiting /<UUID> returned the VLESS configuration/client info for that UUID; that UUID was the tunnel credential, set via env var or top-of-file config in worker-vless.js, and the same UUID appeared in every emitted node link (https://deepwiki.com/zizifn/edgetunnel; https://github.com/zizifn/edgetunnel)
sources: E:/code/Q Proxy/AGENTS.md (repo context for Q Proxy comparison)
takeaways: Adopt the deploy-and-it-works instinct: a professional panel should keep Q Proxy's single-build story (dist/q-proxy.js + dist/_worker.js) but make first-run requirements as close to 'one password + one KV binding' as security allows — edgetunnel proves that paste-deploy, an auto-derived UUID (Q Proxy equivalent: derive from admin password instead of hardcoding), and a no-config tunnel that works before the admin ever opens settings are the entire reason for its 44k-star adoption (https://github.com/cmliu/edgetunnel; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js)

Adopt live-config UX: settings written to KV and effective immediately, with env vars as deployment-time overrides — Q Proxy's validateSettings/saveSettings flow already has the safer core, but should guarantee a 'no redeploy needed' story and consider a beginner/simple mode like edgetunnel's 'I'm a noob' toggle that hides advanced fields (https://deepwiki.com/cmliu/edgetunnel; https://edt-pages.github.io/admin)

Adopt preferred-IP (addip) as a first-class concept but bounded by Q Proxy invariant #10: addresses may only come from user-owned lists (customDomains/cleanIps/cdn.*) — never fetch or hardcode third-party preferred-IP feeds into generation; a cleanIps editor with CF TLS-port validation already matches edgetunnel's port-picker UX without the provenance risk (https://edt-pages.github.io/admin; E:/code/Q Proxy AGENTS.md invariant 10)

Adopt subscription polish: Profile-Update-Interval / Profile-web-page-url / Subscription-Userinfo headers, QR + one-click copy per format, and network self-tests that explain which setting controls which path — these are pure additive UX on top of Q Proxy's existing UA negotiation and per-user sub URLs (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js; https://edt-pages.github.io/admin)

Adopt egress ergonomics: a per-colo default ProxyIP (colo-keyed domain fallback) and documented path/query overrides give instant connectivity on fresh deploys; Q Proxy's failover strategy (chain->direct->proxyIP x8|nat64) is architecturally better but should expose the same 'set one proxy IP, everything works' moment in the panel (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js; E:/code/Q Proxy AGENTS.md)

Adopt KV operation-log viewer with a hard size cap and a usage dashboard — but present numbers as estimates, as both projects' counters are approximations (edgetunnel fakes upload/download from CF request counts; Q Proxy estimates 1 MiB/request) (https://edt-pages.github.io/admin; E:/code/Q Proxy AGENTS.md known gaps)

Must add beyond edgetunnel (already present in Q Proxy, keep non-negotiable): real password hashing + signed revocable sessions + CSRF; a per-user model with quotas/expiry so a leaked node link is not a leaked subscription; SSRF/kill-switch gates; native emitters so node data never transits a third-party subconverter (edgetunnel's converter flow ships every node UUID and preferred IP to an operator-controlled SUBAPI with a merely daily-rotating token) (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js; E:/code/Q Proxy AGENTS.md)

Anti-patterns to explicitly not adopt: MD5MD5(UA+KEY+password) auth cookies (UA-bound, unsalted, offline-crackable, default KEY constant); the 9-way password env fallback that accepts env.UUID as the password; tokens derived deterministically from data inside node share links (MD5MD5(host+UUID)); the /version endpoint that validates UUIDs by first-8-char digit-sum (fuzzy credential check); and the 'kill-detection feature-code' obfuscation + embedded classifier-appeasing prose — an auditable professional panel must stay scanner-honest even where it competes on stealth features (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cmliu/edgetunnel/main/_worker.js)

Evaluated gaps to consider deliberately rather than by omission: XHTTP/gRPC transports are now table stakes in the Chinese client ecosystem (edgetunnel labels WS 'fast', XHTTP 'stable since 2.1.20260811', gRPC 'showy') — worth an ADR before adopting; camouflage homepage and TLS-fragment/0-RTT/ECH node knobs are client-compat features Q Proxy could expose from its node builder without breaking emitter golden tests (https://edt-pages.github.io/admin)

featuresWeLack: Per-user subscription landing page (QR + copy + app deep-links + format downloads) — Marzban/3x-ui have it, Q Proxy serves raw URLs only
One-tap client import deep-links (v2rayng://install-sub?url=, hiddify://import/, sing-box://import-remote-profile?url=, clash://install-config?url=) — zero deep-link coverage in Q Proxy
QR modal/popover in the panel for sub URLs and tokens — Q Proxy requires users to QR-encode externally
Danger Zone section with two-step acknowledge + typed-name confirmation before reset/kill-switch/camouflage disable — Q Proxy destructive actions are one click
First-run wizard with needSetup gate, on-screen language picker (default fa), create-admin-then-auto-login — Q Proxy has setup API but no guided screen
Random-credential reveal card at first run (3x-ui pattern) so password/securePath are captured once by the admin
Usage/expiry progress bars with threshold coloring and clickable resets in user table
Table filter chips (active/expired/over-quota) and dense per-row action buttons
Settings search / command palette — 66 leaf fields across 10 subtabs are only findable by memory
Per-admin language, appearance, timezone preference surface (Cloudflare profile-settings pattern) vs Q Proxy's cookie-seeded qp_lang only
Home as attention surface: expiring users, quota hits, kill-switch state, version-check pin — Q Proxy Home is not an alert triage screen
featuresWeWin: Native bilingual EN/FA panel embedded as HTML strings with RTL — 3x-ui and Marzban bolt on language packs; Cloudflare/Cloudflare Dash offer per-user language prefs but no FA-first single-admin design
UA-negotiated subscription endpoints (?target= override, per ADR-004): one URL already serves the right format to any client — Marzban/3x-ui need per-client format menus
Kill-switch gate runs before WebSocket upgrade (invariant 6) — none of the six panels fail-closed at the protocol gate
Per-user scoping that never merges remoteSubUrls and enforces protocol filters per user — Marzban users share inbounds; Q Proxy's user isolation is architectural

Hardened auth out of the box: PBKDF2 100k with legacy auto-upgrade, HMAC sessions with revocation floor, CSRF header guard, KV-backed login throttle — 3x-ui/Marzban rely on install-time secrets and nginx/IP guards
Camouflage decoy page and WARP/WireGuard config serving (17 formats) — no counterpart in any surveyed panel
Zero-runtime-dependency single-file deploy (dist/q-proxy.js ~470 KB) pasteable into a dashboard — competitors need VPS + docker/systemd + reverse proxy
Emitters are pure functions with golden tests and address composition provably free of hard-coded hosts (invariant 10) — subscription output is auditable, not template-string fragile
panel: Cross-panel UX research for the Q Proxy admin panel (single admin, Home + Settings with 10 subtabs, bilingual EN/FA): six pattern sources surveyed — Tailscale admin console, Cloudflare dash, Uptime Kuma, Alist, 3x-ui, Marzban — with the client deep-link ecosystem (v2rayNG/Hiddify/sing-box) that Marzban-style subscription pages exploit.
screens: Marzban — per-user subscription page (marzban/templates/subscription/index.html, wired via SUBSCRIPTION_PAGE_TEMPLATE + XRAY_SUBSCRIPTION_URL_PREFIX): QR code, copyable sub URL, and one-tap app deep-links (v2rayng://install-sub?url=..., hiddify://import/..., sing-box://import-remote-profile?url=...) that open the client app straight into an imported profile — the single highest-value screen for Q Proxy's per-user token links

Marzban — users table: usage bar + expiry countdown per row, automated share-link/QR generator per user, warning thresholds surfaced (NOTIFY_REACHED_USAGE_PERCENT=80, NOTIFY_DAYS_LEFT=3) — map these exact defaults to amber/red row states in Q Proxy's users table
Marzban — decoy/home template (HOME_PAGE_TEMPLATE) separate from the panel: same idea as Q Proxy's camo.html, but Marzban pairs it with 'dashboard not reachable via IP' hardening guidance

3x-ui — inbounds/clients screen (README-verified): per-client one-click share link, QR code, and subscription URL buttons; live online status; traffic stats with reset controls; search across inbounds and clients; 13 UI languages incl. Persian

3x-ui — install/first-run behavior: installer generates random username, password, and access path and the panel surfaces them once — Q Proxy's setup flow should print its generated admin credentials + sub base URL on a one-time reveal card

3x-ui — built-in subscription server with multiple output formats and custom page templates (docs/custom-subscription-templates.md): template-per-sub-page is the extension point Q Proxy can mirror with its existing emitters (clash-yaml, singbox-json, surge, loon, base64)

Tailscale — Machines page (login.tailscale.com/admin/machines): dense searchable table of devices with per-row quick actions; auth-keys KB confirms per-row Revoke in a bottom table and device key-expiry toggles from the Machines page — model for Q Proxy's user table row actions

Tailscale — admin-console tab structure (Machines / Users / DNS / Access controls / Keys / Settings): flat top tabs, one screen per concern, settings last — validates Q Proxy's Home + Settings(xN) split; the gap is Tailscale pairs every settings tab with the operational object it governs

Cloudflare dash — account > zone two-level nav (concepts doc: 'Accounts, zones, and profiles'): zone list is the home screen, each zone deep-dives with a left subnav — Q Proxy can treat 'users' and 'WARP' as the two zone-like scopes hanging off Home

Cloudflare dash — Agent Lee, an AI co-pilot 'built into the Cloudflare dashboard that helps you navigate, configure, and take actions on Cloudflare services' — the heavyweight version of settings search; a static descriptor-driven index achieves 80% of the value with zero infra

Cloudflare dash — per-user profile settings (docs: 'Customize your Cloudflare dashboard language, appearance, timezone'): language is a profile-level toggle in the header, not buried in Settings — Q Proxy should pin the EN/FA switch in the panel header and persist it to qp_lang

Uptime Kuma — first-run gate (src/pages/Setup.vue): server emits needSetup; unprovisioned visits are redirected to a 'Create your admin account' screen that includes the language selector on the same form, then auto-logs the admin in — exact template for Q Proxy's setup endpoint (which already re-reads KV via loadSettingsFresh)

Alist — settings split into scoped pages (Site, Style, ...) where each page states the blast radius of its fields (site_url drives external links, thumbnails, download URLs; robots.txt and 'allow indexing' default off with a caution note) — discipline worth copying into Q Proxy's 10 subtabs: every field labeled with what breaks if wrong

GitHub (archetype the others converge on) — Settings > Danger Zone: 'Delete this repository' requires two acknowledge clicks plus typing the repo name before the final button enables (docs.github.com deleting-a-repository) — the pattern Q Proxy needs for reset-settings, kill-switch, user deletion, and Telegram unlink
takeaways: Priority 1 — subscription handoff: build a public, token-scoped subscription page (reuse the UA-negotiation seam in src/subscription/) with QR, copy, per-format download links to the existing emitters (?target=clash|singbox|surge|loon), and app deep-link buttons: v2rayng://install-sub?url=<enc>, hiddify://import/<enc>, sing-box://import-remote-profile?url=<enc>, v2box://install-sub?url=<enc>, clash://install-config?url=<enc>. Deep links must be built at runtime from the worker hostname + user token per invariant 10 — never hard-coded addresses. This is exactly what Marzban's SUBSCRIPTION_PAGE_TEMPLATE and 3x-ui's custom-subscription-templates extension point do.

Priority 2 — first-run wizard: Q Proxy's setup endpoint already re-reads KV (TOCTOU-safe). Add a needSetup gate like Uptime Kuma's Setup.vue: redirect unprovisioned visits to a 'Create admin account' screen carrying the EN/FA language selector, auto-login on success, then show a one-time reveal card with the generated sub base URL and a QR (3x-ui's installer-reveals-secrets pattern). Kill the 'log in with defaults' dead end.

Priority 3 — danger zone: group reset-settings, kill-switch toggle, user deletion, Telegram unlink, and camo disable into a visually separated red 'Danger Zone' at the bottom of the relevant subtabs (GitHub pattern): two acknowledge clicks plus typing the object name (setting group or username) before the destructive button enables; wire to the existing AppError/JSON envelope so the API mirrors the UI gate.

Priority 4 — settings search from the descriptor table: SETTING_FIELD_DESCRIPTORS in src/settings/fields.ts already enumerates all 66 leaf fields with the en/fa dictionaries; build a client-side fuzzy index mapping query hits to subtab + field anchor, highlight the field on jump, show 'no results' fallback listing subtab names. Zero new backend surface; the drift test already guarantees the index cannot go stale.

Priority 5 — user table density: per-row actions like 3x-ui/Tailscale — copy sub URL, copy token, QR popover, inline enable/disable toggle (POST to existing users API), usage bar colored by Marzban's proven thresholds (>=80% amber, expired/<3d red), filter chips (all/active/expired/over-quota) above the table instead of a separate page.

Priority 6 — Home as attention surface (Tailscale/CF model): keep Home operational — expiring/expired users, over-quota users, kill-switch state, version-check result, sub URL quick-copy card, WARP account status — so Settings subtabs stay config-only and rarely visited. Single admin means the home screen is the morning triage board.

Priority 7 — header-level language switch (Cloudflare profile-settings pattern): persist choice into qp_lang on every toggle rather than only seeding on first load; mirror Alist's field-level honesty by labeling each settings group with what it breaks (e.g. securePath change invalidates existing panel links).

panel: BPB Panel (github.com/bia-pain-bache/BPB-Worker-Panel, 13.3k stars, homepage https://bia-pain-bache.github.io/BPB-Worker-Panel/) is a single-tenant Cloudflare Workers/Pages panel for VLESS + Trojan + Warp with a private DoH. UI architecture: one SPA-ish static page served at /{securePath}/panel after password/JWT login (src/worker.ts routes: panel, login, sub, telegram, dns-query, proxy-ip, qrcode). The panel is a single scrolling page, NOT tabbed — sections stacked vertically: Admin (usage meter vs 100k/day with red >80%, Update Panel, Delete Panel, Reset Password), "Proxy Settings" as a 10-item accordion (Settings/ports, Telegram Bot, Common, VLESS-Trojan, Xray Fragment, External Raw Configs, Warp General, Warp PRO, Routing Rules, Import-Export) with one Apply/Reset Settings button pair, "Subscriptions" rendered by JS as accordions per sub type (Normal, Fragment, Raw, Warp, Warp Pro), each containing a table of client apps grouped by core (xray, xray-knocker, sing-box, clash, wireguard, amnezia) with per-client QR / copy / download buttons, then DNS over HTTPS (URL + copy), My IP (two-column table: Cloudflare targets vs other targets; IP/country/city/ISP), Supported Clients (table with min versions + download links). Modals: message/confirm, reset-password, QR. Plus a standalone /proxy-ip page listing public proxy IPs by region/ISP with worker-vantage TCP latency test. How a user gets configs: deploy via BPB Wizard (web https://wizard.bpb-panel.workers.dev or CLI) → open /{securePath}/panel → forced password-set on first visit → adjust accordions → Apply Settings → scroll to Subscriptions → pick type+client → scan server-generated QR (POST /qrcode returns PNG), copy URL (./sub/<type>?app=<core>, sing-box gets a sing-box://import-remote-profile deep link), or download (not for Raw) → re-update subscription after any setting change; Telegram bot can also deliver subs/QR/config files. Subscription rows carry special auto-configs: Best Ping (retests every 30s), Best Fragment (18 variants), Smart Fragment, Workerless, Warp/WoW/Best-Ping variants, chained (link icon) configs, and flags F (fragment), C (custom CDN), D (custom domain). Settings organization: flat accordions, Apply/Reset, reset preserves UUID/password/securePath, Import/Export via .dat file or a peer /sub/share-settings link (excludes UUID/password/path). WARP handling: two auto-managed accounts (Warp + Warp-on-Warp), Renew Accounts button (POST panel/update-warp), Warp General accordion (IPv4 remote DNS, Endpoints + downloadable scanner script, Fake DNS, IPv6, Best Interval 10-90s, Reserved Bytes), Warp PRO accordion (noise per client family: MahsaNG quic/random/custom-hex; v2ray base64/string/random/hex with count; Clash/Amnezia count+size min/max) and zip downloads for WireGuard/Amnezia/WG Tunnel. Fragment/normal: Fragment modes low/medium/high/severe/custom (default length 100-200, delay 1-1, packets tlshello; caps 500/30ms; maxSplit), fragment sub for Xray (F flag) and sing-box >=1.12; Normal sub applies all panel settings + routing. QR flow: per-client button → server-side PNG via /qrcode → modal titled with sub label. Localization: panel UI is English-only (<html lang="en">, no i18n dictionary); bilingualism exists only in docs (mkdocs EN + FA alternate sites, README_fa.md). Auth: single password → JWT cookie; no 2FA, no per-user identities, no kill switch, no IP allowlist.

takeaways: BPB is a single-tenant power tool for the Iran-censorship scenario: its whole UI funnels one admin toward Best-Ping/Best-Fragment/Warp-Pro self-optimizing configs, while Q Proxy is a small-team sharing panel (per-user links, quotas, expiry, TOTP, kill switch). These are different products; the gap lists above are directional, not defects on either side.

Highest-value BPB features worth adopting in Q Proxy: (1) Best-Ping-style auto-select configs, (2) a richer Telegram bot (deliver subs/QR/usage), (3) in-panel self-update, (4) more routing rule presets (porn/phishing/cryptominer blocks, country bypass). All are additive without touching Q's wire formats.

Q's clearest structural advantages over BPB: real multi-user scoping, TOTP 2FA, kill switch gated before WS upgrade, IP allowlist, VMess+SS protocols, and native Surge/Loon/Quantumult X emitters — none of which BPB offers anywhere in its docs or settings schema (settings.ts defines only vless,trojan).

BPB's panel UI is a single English-only scrolling page with accordions; Q Proxy's tabbed Home/Settings shell with 10 subtabs, bilingual EN/FA dicts, theme toggle, and onboarding wizard is materially more navigable and internationalized.

Both panels share the same skeleton features: secure-path URLs, private DoH endpoint, ECH, fragment presets (low/medium/high/severe/custom), NAT64 proxy-IP mode, custom CDN fronting, chain proxy (BPB's supports more upstream formats), fallback/camouflage page, import/export settings, Warp endpoint management, and a proxy-IP tester (different vantages: BPB worker-side page, Q browser-side card).

Architecture note: BPB tunnels Warp/WireGuard through Xray/sing-box subscription pipelines and the Worker, while Q Proxy serves WARP configs directly per account with zero Worker traffic — Q's approach scales better on the 100k/day request budget that BPB itself documents as its main limitation (https://github.com/bia-pain-bache/BPB-Worker-Panel#limitations).

Caveat: feature 'absence' claims for BPB are based on its full README, docs site (all 20+ pages fetched), settings schema (src/types/settings.ts), and panel assets (index.html/script.js) reviewed on 2026-02-14; a future BPB release could add any of them.
